```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The AI tool you worked with knows what it just did, so it can draft the log
entry. You then review the draft, which is faster than writing it. Drafted
entries are saved with outcome `pending`, are left out of AI-use statements,
and are flagged by `check_ai_log()` until you review them.

`create_ai_log()` puts the instructions for AI tools in
`ai-use/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md`. They say when to draft an entry, how to choose
`error_visibility`, to record only checks actually run, and to leave
`human_decisions` for you.

## Coding agents

Agents that run commands in your project (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot's
agent, Codex and similar) log directly with `Rscript`. Point them to the
instructions from the file they read at the start of each session, such as
`CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`:

```markdown
At the end of each work session, follow ai-use/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md.
```

## Chat apps

Chat apps such as Claude or ChatGPT on the web or desktop usually can't
write to your project. Instead, the instructions ask them to end the session
with an R call for you to paste. Add the contents of
`ai-use/AI-INSTRUCTIONS.md` to the app's custom instructions (or a Claude
Project's instructions), or paste it into the chat when you want an entry.
The app then replies with something like:

```r
ailogR::add_ai_tool("Claude", "Anthropic", "Opus 5.5", "web")
ailogR::log_ai(
  task = "Bayesian model for reservoir drought vulnerability in brms",
  tool_id = "claude-opus-5.5", research_stage = "data_analysis",
  error_visibility = "silent",
  how_checked = "none",
  logged_by = "ai")
```

`add_ai_tool()` does nothing if the tool is already listed.

## Reviewing drafts

```{r}
library(ailogR)
project <- file.path(tempdir(), "drafts")
create_ai_log(project)
add_ai_tool("Claude", "Anthropic", "Opus 5.5", "cli_agent", path = project)
log_ai("Join gauge and chemistry tables by site and date",
       tool_id = "claude-opus-5.5", research_stage = "data_curation",
       error_visibility = "silent",
       how_checked = "Row counts before and after the join match",
       evidence = "R/join_sites.R", logged_by = "ai", path = project)
check_ai_log(project)
```

Interactively, `edit_ai_log()` lists drafts first. For each, it shows what
the tool recorded, asks what you decided and the outcome, and then lets you
correct any field, such as an `error_visibility` you disagree with or a
check you want to add. With arguments:

```{r}
edit_ai_log(1,
            human_decisions = "Chose to keep unmatched dates as NA",
            how_checked = "Row counts match; checked 20 joined rows against the raw files",
            outcome = "modified", path = project)
```

The entry keeps `logged_by = "ai"`, so the log shows it was drafted by an AI
tool and reviewed by a person.
